newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai markets hit by economy, political worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai markets hit by economy, political worries.

text.p: Thai markets took another pounding on Wednesday as foreign investors took flight from the baht and sold stocks on fears over the economy and the political situation.

Stocks in Bangkok tumbled 4.35 percent by the lunch break as foreign investors led renewed selling of blue-chip stocks on concern about the sluggish economy and market pressure on the baht, brokers said.

The SET index plunged 26.11 points to 574.13 on moderate 2.09 billion baht trade. The SET-50 index retreated 2.36 points to 41.94. The main composite index hovered at its lowest level since mid-June 1989.
"We got a lot of selling orders from foreign clients who partly reacted to the currency market's shift to the dollar from the baht," said a foreign broker.
An analyst at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities said expected weak first quarter earnings of most telecommunication companies also prompted morning selling.
Brokers said investors are still concerned about the sluggish economy which is expected to grow less than six percent this year.
Some currency dealers said they believed the Bank of Thailand had intervened to defend the baht in the Singapore market during midday on Wednesday but the central bank did not confirm it.
The baht fell to 26.250-26.300 to the dollar before it recovered to 26.030-26.080 at 0656 GMT. The central bank fixed the baht/dollar midrate at 25.86 on Wednesday against 25.88 on Tuesday.
"I heard that the central bank intervened, otherwise the baht could not stage such a comeback," a Thai bank dealer.
Dealers said their Singapore counterparts quoted baht selling offers in big $100 million lots against $10-30 million deals in normal market conditions.
Rising concerns about the slowing Thai economy and rumours of political turmoil within the cabinet, seen hampering effective monetary policy, triggered baht sales for the dollar.
Dealers said the Bank of Thailand fixing the mid-rate at 25.86 did not prevent the rate slipping to 26.03.
"There was a lot of stop-loss and panic-selling which caused the market to trade 20 satangs above the fixing," a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore said.
"The demand for the dollar is much stronger today. Players in Hong Kong and Singapore were heavily bidding the dollar (by selling baht)," said one dealer at a local bank in Bangkok.
Thai prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh reiterated on Tuesday there would be no change in economic ministers and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan will continue in his post and maintain authority.
"Amnuay will still have authority in economic affairs and there will be no change in the economic ministers," Chavalit said after the weekly cabinet meeting.
His comments come during renewed rumours that Amnuay was due to resign following a conflict with a major partner in Chavalit's coalition.

On Monday, Amnuay had also dismissed market speculation that the Chart Pattana Party, a major coalition party in the government, was unhappy with his performance during the administration's six months in office.
Some members in Chavalit's government suggested late last week that Amnuay could help halt the Thai economic slowdown and a prolonged stock market decline by stepping down.
